speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are concerned about a newborn with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting. To help me assess the situation, could you tell me the baby's age in days and whether they have passed any meconium stools yet?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient is six hours old with bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance, which suggests a distal obstruction. I need to rule out malrotation with midgut volvulus, a surgical emergency. Have you observed any abdominal distension or signs of peritonitis, and has an abdominal X-ray or ultrasound been performed yet?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Doctor
text: Bilious vomiting in a newborn is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise, so I need to visualize the anatomy immediately. REQUEST TEST: Upper_GI_Series

speaker: Doctor
text: A normal Upper GI series effectively rules out malrotation and midgut volvulus, shifting our focus to other causes of distal obstruction like intestinal atresia. Given the bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance since birth, I need to see the abdominal radiograph to look for the classic "double bubble" sign of duodenal atresia or other dilated loops. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray
